kicker: Laya vs Jev, a dinosaur race

scenes.headline: How a dinosaur race asks two models different questions
scenes.sub: Laya answers locally, Jev over the network, and the harness adapts to each.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pretzel! This repo races two decision models through Chrome's dinosaur game. Here's how the harness works.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: The harness describes the world as it will be when each player's answer lands, so a slower model gets a different question.
scenes.mark: a slower model gets a different question
scenes.say: The harness describes the world as it will be when each answer lands. So a slower model gets a different question.

scenes.title: Why one question at a time fails

parts.note: one round trip to the hosted Jev API
parts.say: One round trip to Jev's hosted API takes about three hundred and seventy milliseconds.
A frame lasts sixteen point six seven.

parts.note: a jump window is 13 to 26 frames
parts.say: So one answer costs twenty-two frames: about the whole window in which a jump works.

steps.say: Each move, a planner simulates the physics ahead, using this player's own measured latency.
It writes the question: jump, duck or run, each labelled best, safe or unsafe.

steps.note: at most 4 questions per round trip: a turn every 6 frames
steps.say: The model answers with probabilities. With several questions in flight, even the slow player gets a turn every six frames.
The pilot throws away answers whose premise went stale, and plays the rest.

left.title: Laya: answers in 2 frames
left.say: On one frame, Laya is told the cacti are a hundred and seventy-two pixels away: waiting is best.

right.title: Jev: answers in 22 frames
right.say: Jev is told seventy pixels: jumping is best. Each prompt is right about the world its answer lands in.

scenes.title: Snapshots where all three moves are marked safe
scenes.note: 122 snapshots; the same question for both on only 13.9%
scenes.say: Over the repo's own snapshots, the two get the same question only thirteen point nine percent of the time. Jev's are more forced, so easier.

steps.say: The repo's own arena screenshot: Laya local on the left, Jev hosted on the right.
Its best-move bar reads seventy-one against eighty-nine percent. Those were two different exams, and the eighty-nine belongs to the easier one.

scenes.text: A prompt adapted to each caller makes the score caller-dependent. To compare models, ask them identical questions.

recap: One Jev round trip is about 22 frames
Each prompt is built from its player's latency
Same question on only 13.9% of snapshots
scenes.say: To recap: latency shapes the prompt, and the prompt shapes the score.
